title: CultureLLM: Incorporating Cultural Differences into Large Language Models
findings: CultureLLM provides more direct and accurate classifications of religiously-charged hate speech compared to baseline models like ChatGPT. In a German language case study, CultureLLM correctly identified a sentence mentioning 'muslimische Frauen' (Muslim women) and '#Islamisierung' as hate speech, while ChatGPT's response was more evasive and did not make a definitive classification.

measurement_description: The benchmark measures attitudes towards religious values and the ability to detect hate speech targeting religious groups. The seed data from the World Value Survey (WVS) includes questions on topics such as conflicts between science and religion. The downstream evaluation includes a fine-grained hate speech detection task with a specific category for religion.
